meta.title: OpenBooks — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: OpenBooks: old Dutch building and engineering textbooks by Wattjes, Gugel, Vandepitte and others, scanned and free to read online, without an account.

header.label: Historical building literature
header.desc: Anyone who renovates, restores or assesses an existing building needs to know how it was built back then. That knowledge sits in textbooks that have been out of print for decades. OpenBooks scans them and puts them online for free: leaf through the original pages and zoom in on the drawings, without an account.
header.issuesBtn: Suggest a book or report an error

notice.text: Free to use: we only publish books that, as far as we can tell, are free of copyright. Is that not the case for a book? Let us know at info@open-aec.com.

features.label: Collection and reader
features.heading: Knowledge you can no longer buy
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

collection.title: Textbooks that are almost impossible to find second-hand
collection.desc: The ten volumes of Constructies van Gebouwen by Wattjes, the Architectonische Vormenleer by Gugel, Berekening van Constructies by Vandepitte and more: from a treatise of 1670 to the Dutch concrete regulations of 1974.

find.title: The right book, fast
find.desc: Filter by architecture, construction, calculations, steel, timber, regulations or classical, or search by title and author. Every book shows its year and number of pages.

reader.title: Leaf through it like the real book
reader.desc: Open a book and page through the original scans with the arrows or the arrow keys, from cover to back. Use Go to to jump straight to the page number from a reference.

zoom.title: Zoom in on every drawing
zoom.desc: Enlarge a page up to five times and pan across it, so the dimensions, bonds and profiles in the old detail drawings become easy to read.

wattjes.title: Prof. J.G. Wattjes (10 volumes)
wattjes.desc: Constructies van Gebouwen: walls, chimneys, foundations, windows and doors, floors, vaults, stairs, roof structures and more.

gugel.title: Prof. E.H. Gugel
gugel.desc: Architectonische Vormenleer (1880): the plates and the text on architectural forms.

vandepitte.title: Prof. D. Vandepitte (3 volumes)
vandepitte.desc: Berekening van Constructies: structural analysis theory in three extensive volumes.

potma.title: Ir. A.P. Potma and Ir. J.E. de Vries
potma.desc: Staalconstructies: theory, calculation and execution of steel load-bearing structures.

zwiers.title: L. Zwiers
zwiers.desc: Handboek Houtconstructies: the handbook for timber structures.

bosboom.title: Symon Bosboom
bosboom.desc: Cort onderwys van de vyf colommen (1670): a treatise on the five classical orders by the city stonemason of Dordrecht.

codes.title: Building regulations
codes.desc: The Dutch reinforced concrete regulations G.B.V. 1950 and the concrete regulations VB 1974.

more.title: And more
more.desc: Bernoullis Vademecum for the civil engineer, a book on panel doors and a German chapter on structural calculations.

zoom.title: Zoom and pan
zoom.desc: From 50 to 500 percent, with the buttons, the mouse wheel or the + and - keys.

browse.title: Page through
browse.desc: With the arrows next to the page or the arrow keys on your keyboard.

goto.title: Go to page
goto.desc: Type a page number and the reader jumps straight to it.

categories.title: Categories and search
categories.desc: Filter by seven categories or search by title and author.

ocr.title: Text recognition
ocr.desc: Books whose text has already been recognised carry an OCR label. Searching inside the text comes later.

free.title: Free and without an account
free.desc: No subscription and no login: open the site and start reading.

github.title: All scans on GitHub
github.desc: Every scanned page is an image in the public repository, including books that are not in the reader yet.

contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.desc: Do you have an old textbook that belongs here? Suggest it on GitHub.

rights.title: Free of copyright
rights.desc: Only books that, as far as we can tell, are free of copyright.

whatsnew.label: Latest developments
whatsnew.title: A reader of its own and new scans
whatsnew.desc: OpenBooks has no releases: the collection grows book by book. This is what was added in 2026.

german.title: A German chapter
german.desc: Fifteen scans of a chapter on the origin, consequences and checking of structural calculations.

host.title: Its own address
host.desc: The collection now lives at open-books.open-aec.com, and the scans come straight from the repository.

viewer.title: Reader with zoom
viewer.desc: Page through, zoom in up to 500 percent and jump straight to a page.

site.title: A website for the collection
site.desc: All books in one place, with categories and search by title and author.

cost.a: Nothing. You need no account or subscription: open the site and start reading.

rights.q: Can these books simply be put online?
rights.a: We only publish books that, as far as we can tell, are free of copyright. With old books that is not always easy to establish. If a book is still under copyright after all, let us know at info@open-aec.com and we will take it down right away.

which.q: Are all books in the reader?
which.a: Not yet. The reader now shows thirteen books. The scans of the other books, such as the remaining volumes of Wattjes and Vandepitte, are already on GitHub and are being added step by step.

search.q: Can I search the text of the books?
search.a: Not yet. For now you search by title and author. The text of a few books has already been recognised with OCR; searching the text of all books is planned.

lang.q: What language are the books in?
lang.a: Almost all are in Dutch; there is one German chapter. The website itself is in Dutch too.

contribute.q: I have an old textbook. Can it be added?
contribute.a: Gladly. Suggest the book on GitHub, with its title, author and year. The wish list includes the other books by Wattjes, older concrete standards and old building magazines.

reuse.a: The scans are there to be used: in a report, a renovation plan or a lesson. Please credit the book and its author as the source. All scans are available as separate images on GitHub.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: Deliberately simple: scans as images, a reader in the browser and everything in one public repository.

web.title: Reader in the browser
web.desc: A single web page built with React. There is nothing to install.

scans.title: Scans in Git
scans.desc: Every page is an image in the repository, with its full history.

deploy.title: Published automatically
deploy.desc: A change in the repository appears on open-books.open-aec.com by itself.

scripts.title: Python scripts
scripts.desc: Helper scripts number and rename the pages of a book.
